title: Bibingka: Baked Coconut Rice Cake with Salted Egg on Banana Leaf
summary: A coconut rice-flour cake baked on banana leaf, topped with salted egg and finished with butter and sugar under a hot grill.
equipment: 23 cm cast-iron frying pan or round cake tin

ingredients.item: unsalted butter, melted, for the pan

ingredients.note: use a gluten-free one if needed

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
salted duck egg, cooked, peeled and sliced

steps.title: Prepare the pan
steps.text: Heat the oven to 180 °C (160 °C fan). Soften the banana leaf by passing it briefly over a flame or dipping it in hot water, line the pan and brush with the 15 g butter. Without a leaf, butter the pan and line the base with baking paper.

steps.title: Mix the batter
steps.text: Whisk both rice flours, the baking powder, salt and sugar in one bowl. In the other, whisk the coconut milk, eggs and 60 g melted butter, then pour into the dry mix and whisk until completely smooth; rice flour has no gluten, so you cannot overmix it.

steps.title: First bake
steps.text: Pour the batter into the pan and bake for 15 min, until the edges have just set. Waiting stops the egg slices sinking.

steps.title: Add the salted egg
steps.text: Arrange the salted egg slices over the surface and bake for 15-20 min more, until risen and golden and a skewer in the centre comes out clean.

steps.title: Butter and char
steps.text: Brush with the remaining butter, scatter over the tablespoon of sugar and grill (broiler) on high for 2-3 min. Watch closely: you want dark speckles of caramel, not burnt sugar.

steps.title: Rest and serve
steps.text: Leave in the pan for 10 min so the crumb sets, then cut into wedges and serve warm.

tips: Salted duck eggs are sold cooked in Asian grocers; if yours are raw, simmer them for 10 min first.
A common mistake is grilling too long: the sugar goes from golden to burnt in seconds.
The banana leaf adds a gentle tea-like aroma, but the cake is still good without it.
Check the label of the baking powder if you need the cake to be gluten-free.
Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Best eaten warm on the day. Keep covered in the fridge for up to 2 days and reheat in a 180 °C (160 °C fan) oven for 8-10 min until hot through.
